newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Komercni shares plunge in mood of pessimism.
newsitem.headline: Czech Komercni shares plunge in mood of pessimism.

text.p: Shares in the largest Czech commercial bank Komercni Banka a.s. plunged on market pessimism about the prospects for the Czech banking sector and general macroeconomic prospects, dealers said on Monday.
Just after mid-session during continuous trading on the Prague bourse, Komercni's shares were down 81 crowns, 3.7 percent, to 2,085.
"Weak first quarter results imply that net earnings growth this year will be limited. We have downgraded Komercni from buy to hold," ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said in a report to investors.
Last week, Komercni posted consolidated pre-tax profits of one billion crowns for the first quarter from 1.3 billion in the same period in 1996, according to international accounting standards.
ABN-AMRO's Eugene Klerk said the bank would be hurt by the slowdown in the Czech economy, especially the continued need to make large provisions against bad or doubtful loans.
Generally, Klerk said Czech major issues -- Komercni accounts for 11 percent of the PX50 index's capitalisation -- would continue to suufer by the absence of foreign buying.
"I can't see any reason, macro or micro, why investors should put money into the Czech Republic," he told Reuters.
